cards.explanation: The answer is three, friends. Jesus says, “…they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat.” Three days with nothing to eat, and He doesn't brush it off. He says right out, “I have compassion for this crowd…” That's the heart of this whole story.

The answer is that they will faint along the way, friends. Jesus says, “If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way.” He adds, “For some of them have come a great distance.” I think He's looking down the road, and that's what compassion looks like: already thinking about the trip home.

The answer is True, bakers. Jesus says, “For some of them have come a great distance.” So this isn't just a neighborhood crowd. Some of these folks traveled far, and they're now far from a meal too. That makes sending them home hungry an even harder walk.

The answer is that they ask where anyone could find enough bread to feed them, friends. The disciples ask, “Where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people?” They're looking around at empty land and a huge crowd. I think I'd be asking the same thing. Good thing Jesus has a plan.
The answer is seven, bakers. Jesus asks, “How many loaves do you have?” and they reply, “Seven.” Seven loaves for a crowd that big. I've stretched a batch before, but never THAT far, friends.

The answer is sit down on the ground, friends. The text says Jesus “…instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground.” Nothing is handed out yet. First the whole crowd settles in, and then He takes the loaves. I think a seated crowd means everybody's getting fed.

The answer is thanks, bakers. The text says Jesus “…took the seven loaves, gave thanks and broke them…” He gives thanks first, with seven loaves in His hands in front of a huge crowd. Then comes the breaking. That's worth remembering the next time you face a table that looks too small.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus broke the loaves and gave them to His disciples “…to set before the people.” Then the text says they “…distributed them to the crowd.” So the disciples carried the bread out to the crowd. They're in the middle of it, handing out food that came from seven loaves.
The answer is False, bakers. The text says, “The people ate and were satisfied…” Everybody, not just the folks up front. Seven loaves and a few small fish, and that crowd walked away full.

The answer is True, friends. They started with seven loaves, and the disciples “…picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.” Seven in, seven baskets out, after a whole crowd was satisfied. I'd call that a pretty good return.

The answer is the district of Dalmanutha, bakers. The text says Jesus “…immediately got into the boat with His disciples and went to the district of Dalmanutha.” Right after the crowd leaves, He's off.

The answer is a sign from heaven, friends. The Pharisees were “…testing Him by demanding from Him a sign from heaven.” The text says they came and began to argue with Jesus. A sign is what they demanded.

The answer is False, bakers, and Jesus is clear about it. He says, “Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.” No promise, no maybe later. He sighed deeply in His spirit first, so I think this one weighed on Him.

The answer is one loaf, friends. The text says the disciples “…had forgotten to take bread, except for one loaf they had with them in the boat.” One loaf for a boatful of disciples. That's a tight lunch, bakers.

The answer is their leaven, bakers. Jesus cautions them, “Watch out! Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod.” Herod was ruler of Galilee (Luke 3:1), and Jesus names him right alongside the Pharisees. Leaven is what makes dough rise, and that's the word Jesus picks.

The answer is True, friends. The text says Jesus was “Aware of their conversation…” The disciples were talking with one another about having no bread, and He knew it. Then He asks them, “Why are you debating about having no bread?”

The answer is that they still do not understand, bakers. Jesus asks, “Do you still not see or understand?” and goes on, “‘Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear?’…” In this very passage, seven loaves fed the crowd, and now the disciples are debating about having no bread.

The answer is twelve, friends. Jesus asks, “When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” and they answer, “Twelve.” Five loaves went out, and twelve baskets came back. The disciples knew the number, and then Jesus asks, “Do you still not understand?”

The answer is False, bakers. After they answer “Twelve” and “Seven,” Jesus asks, “Do you still not understand?” That's where the passage ends. Jesus doesn't say they finally get it. He ends on the question.
